OpenAI Rilis Images 2.6: ChatGPT Kini Bisa Bikin GIF, Generasi Gambar 50% Lebih Cepat

OpenAI released Images 2.6 on November 4, 2026, with animated GIF output and stored reference pictures for ChatGPT users. Two additional models reach developers through the API, called GPT-Image-2.6 Flare and GPT-Image-2.6 Sunburst. Images 2.6 reaches Codex , ChatGPT and the developer API, and OpenAI says each now produces pictures 50% faster. Users across those products generate 4 billion images every week, or over half a billion each day by the company’s math. Rollout is global, covering every ChatGPT and Codex subscription tier across web, desktop and mobile apps. Within ChatGPT, a text prompt or still photo can now become a looping animation. People can change how quickly the GIF plays, tweak frames one by one and post the finished clip to cycle endlessly. GIFS! With ChatGPT Images 2.6, turn a prompt or image into an animated GIF. Adjust the speed, edit individual frames, and share it on repeat. https://t.co/i4hsLoapx3

Marketers and creators are the main audience OpenAI has in mind for GIFs. Suggested projects include a campaign mascot in motion, reaction memes for social feeds and animated storyboards that sketch out how a character moves before any video gets filmed. A second ChatGPT addition keeps reference images of the user, a pet or a recurring character on file. Stored pictures can be dropped into later projects with no fresh upload. Consistency of a person or character across a series of images is the goal. Sample animations in the announcement came from the creative platform OpenArt and star a big-headed cartoon office worker drawn in chibi style. One clip shows the character sobbing as the market line plunges, and the other has the worker cheering and flinging paper banknotes skyward. Each prompt requested one sprite sheet holding six sequential frames for a looping GIF, arranged as a grid two rows high and three columns wide. Every panel had to match in size, the camera stayed fixed, and the outfit, desk and character could not change between frames. Frame six also had to transition back toward frame one so the loop would restart cleanly. Flare is the quicker of the pair and can finish a picture in as few as six seconds on its low quality setting, OpenAI wrote. Posters, product shots and other professional layouts also come out better arranged with Flare, the company said. Sunburst targets work that demands finer detail, and on its medium and high quality settings it keeps a subject steadier through round after round of edits. Developers can now annotate an image to guide changes and export results as vector SVG files that stay crisp at any size, according to OpenAI’s community forum post . Separate model cards for each, Flare and Sunburst, now appear on OpenAI’s developer documentation, alongside a page with image generation pricing . No prices appear on the launch page itself. Coco Mao, CEO and co-founder of OpenArt, called GIFs “the native language of social media.” At Figma Weave, creative director Itay Schiff said the update “brings speed and creative control together,” and the workflow product is bringing the model into its lineup. Picsart, an early access customer whose artwork appears in OpenAI’s forum post, pointed to “more accurate results, better character consistency, and faster generations.”
